name: Julia code injection via eval(Meta.parse) or shell -c
attack_scenario: user_code = "run(`rm -rf /`)" is compiled and executed; typed parse(Int, ...) only ever yields an integer or throws.
negative_test_hint: feed user_code = "run(`rm -rf /`)" and assert it is rejected or handled by typed parsing instead of being eval'd

exemplar.explanation: Julia backtick commands escape interpolation safely, so the real footguns are eval(Meta.parse(...))/include_string, which compile and run arbitrary code, and explicitly wrapping a shell (sh -c $x), which defeats the automatic escaping by making the interpolated value a shell script.
